hero.tagline: Parallel development for the agent era.
hero.subtitle: One Mac-native window. Many worktrees. Every agent.

multi_project.title: Many projects. One window.
multi_project.lead: Side-projects, day-job repos, agents-on-loan — all of them live as first-class Projects in the same tree. No more Cmd-Tab between five Finder windows, no more "which terminal was claude in?". Open touch-code and the whole landscape is already there.
multi_project.stat: Built for 1–20 active projects at once.

worktree.title: Built on git worktrees.
worktree.lead: Every Worktree is a real on-disk checkout — its own directory, its own terminal, its own agent. Spin one up per task in a single command; merge back without stashing, without context-switching the repo, without losing the dev server that's still running on a sibling branch.
worktree.punchline: A branch in a directory, not in a stash.

extensions.title: Extensible where it matters.
extensions.lead: Five integration points the rest of the app is wired around. Each one starts from the same Project / Worktree address, so the same shortcut means the same thing everywhere.

commands.title: Custom commands & shortcuts
commands.body: Bind any per-project script to a chord — `⌃R` runs the right setup.sh whether you're in main, fix/race-cond or a brand-new worktree.

ide.title: Open in your editor
ide.body: VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Xcode, Sublime — auto-detected and routed by Project. One keystroke from any worktree to the right window.

git.title: Git Viewer overlay
git.body: `⌘⌥G` summons a full diff / history pane on top of the terminal without shrinking the panes below a usable width.

agents.title: Agents View
agents.body: Every running agent — Claude Code, Codex, pi, opencode — surfaces in one panel with live state: waiting, working, finished, idle. Click a row, you land in that pane.

pr.title: Pull request status
pr.body: PR snapshots pulled in batch from `gh`. State, checks rollup and reviewers ride on every worktree row, surface again in the titlebar status slot.

cta.title: Get touch-code.
cta.sub: Drag into /Applications. The tc shim installs itself on first launch.
